reason_no_fresh_inference: Epoch25959 is active on the only host with the native runtime. Recovered completed runs and inert framework tests are sufficient for this scoped investigation.

parity_evidence.interpretation: Observed baseline variation disproves an unconditional deterministic/bit-identical claim for this runtime. It does not identify which stage causes variation or demonstrate a warm-path distribution shift.

findings.evidence: Best recovered48-candidate run75.4s versus99.5s baseline is1.32x. Doubling48 to96 workers gives only1.04x throughput. Executor-patched48-candidate batch91.9066s versus99.0926s baseline batch is1.078x; one uncontrolled run, not an equivalence result.

findings.reason: Only the full sequence plus runtime/model/settings/tool identity can key a reusable measured result. A shared framework is not an identical input. Returning cached bytes preserves that recorded observation, not a fresh stochastic rerun. Cache reads must never count as independent repeats or fresh evaluations.

findings.limitation: No cache lookup latency or actual workload hit-rate benchmark performed. A workload of fresh unique inputs has no such gain.

findings.reason: Current pinned live profile is CPU-only. GPU/batched kernels and refinement are numerical-path changes; matching weights/seeds/precision does not establish bit identity.

The current dispatcher already profiles independent inputs concurrently. Additional nested CPU workers can oversubscribe. Existing evidence does not attribute a large share of wall time to postprocessing.
No recovered disk-wait or physical-I/O breakdown supports this as a dominant cost. Test bounded per-job tmpfs only after measuring I/O; memory competes with roughly1.4GB profile processes.

findings.proposal: match executor width to admitted live profiles
findings.reason: Pinned service acquires a TNP semaphore then uses asyncio.to_thread. The old private asyncio.run loop uses the default executor capped at32 threads on its Python runtime, despite48 profile slots. The candidate patch owns a fresh loop and pool sized to the existing resource-bounded worker count; it does not alter backend commands, model or gates.

patch_scope: Add run_develop() owning one loop and one bounded ThreadPoolExecutor
Route live worker measure_batch through it
Leave cached_develop and its legacy capacity behavior unchanged
No caching, model, seed, precision, GPU or scientific acceptance changes

validation.new_test_scope: Real pinned compute_tnp_profile_async AST with48 inert profiles rendezvousing, preserving output order; caller-loop isolation; owned-thread shutdown; errors; fresh repeats; invalid widths; empty batch

next_measurement: Between live epochs, compare the private executor change against baseline using identical input cohorts and randomized run order; measure completed profiles/sec, errors, memory and live responsiveness.
Record preprocessing, prediction, refinement and metric/IO timing separately before optimizing them.
Persistent model reuse and GPU batching require their own stochastic-baseline versus candidate comparison; never claim exact parity unless measured at the required artifact level.
